# `supabase/permissive-policy`: Overly permissive Row Level Security policy

<!-- Generated by `npm run docs:rules` from the rule metadata in src/rules/. Edit only the
     hand:* regions here; everything else comes from the rule and is overwritten. -->

| Family   | Default severity | GitHub security-severity | CWE                                                                                                                    |
| -------- | ---------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| supabase | high             | 8.0                      | [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html), [CWE-639](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/639.html) |

Individual findings can have a lower or higher severity than the default, and each has a
confidence (high, medium or low). Both are explained below.

## What it detects

<!-- hand:detects -->

RLS policies on exposed tables that admit every row:

- `USING (true)` / `WITH CHECK (true)` (and equivalent always-true expressions);
- conditions that only check that the caller is logged in (`auth.uid() IS NOT NULL`,
  `auth.role() = 'authenticated'`, `TO authenticated USING (true)`).

Severity depends on the command, the audience and the table:

| Policy                                                      | Anyone (`anon` / `public`)                        | Any logged-in user           |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `UPDATE` / `DELETE` / `ALL`                                 | critical                                          | high                         |
| `INSERT`                                                    | high (medium on obvious public-submission tables) | medium (low on those tables) |
| `SELECT` on personal or sensitive-looking tables            | high                                              | medium                       |
| `SELECT` on other tables                                    | medium                                            | low                          |
| `SELECT` on obvious reference data (countries, plans, tags) | low, low confidence                               | not reported                 |

<!-- /hand:detects -->

## Why it matters

RLS is on, but a policy admits every row: USING (true) / WITH CHECK (true), or a condition that only checks the caller is logged in (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL, auth.role() = 'authenticated'). For UPDATE/DELETE that lets any visitor or any user edit and wipe everyone's data. For INSERT, anyone can create rows on behalf of others. For SELECT on personal data, everything is readable. Read-only access to obvious reference data (countries, plans, tags) is reported at low severity so you can confirm it is intentional.

## Messages

What a finding from this rule says (parameters in braces):

- Policy "{policy}" lets anyone, including anonymous visitors, {command} every row of {table}.
- Policy "{policy}" lets any logged-in user {command} every row of {table}, not just their own.
- Policy "{policy}" lets anyone, including anonymous visitors, insert arbitrary rows into {table}.
- Policy "{policy}" lets any logged-in user insert rows into {table} with any owner or values (WITH CHECK does not tie rows to the caller).
- Policy "{policy}" makes every row of {table} readable by anyone, including anonymous visitors.
- Policy "{policy}" makes every row of {table} readable by any logged-in user.

## How to fix

Scope every write policy to the row owner, in both USING (which rows) and WITH CHECK (what rows may become). Use separate policies per command. Prefer "TO authenticated" plus an ownership check over "TO anon/public".

### Vulnerable

```sql
create policy "Enable update for users" on public.orders
  for update to authenticated
  using (true) with check (true);  -- any user can edit any order
```

### Fixed

```sql
create policy "Users update their own orders" on public.orders
  for update to authenticated
  using ((select auth.uid()) = user_id)
  with check ((select auth.uid()) = user_id);
```

## False positives and limitations

<!-- hand:false-positives -->

- **Public read data** is legitimate: a blog's `posts`, a product catalogue, reference
  tables. These are reported at medium or low severity so you can confirm the intent, then
  suppress with the reason (for example "published posts are public by design").
- **Public submission tables** (contact forms, waitlists) legitimately allow anonymous
  `INSERT`; they are reported lower. Make sure `SELECT` is not also open.
- **Only syntactic checks:** a condition that looks scoped but is wrong (`owner_id = owner_id`,
  a join that leaks rows) is not reported. A clean result does not prove the policies are
  correct.
- **Limitations:** column-level privileges are not modelled; policies created outside
  migrations are invisible.

<!-- /hand:false-positives -->

## How to suppress

Only suppress a finding after confirming it is safe. Put the directive on the line above
the reported line (or use `vibeguard-ignore-line` on the line itself, or
`vibeguard-ignore-file` anywhere in the file). The reason is required: a directive without
one suppresses nothing and is reported.

```sql
-- vibeguard-ignore-next-line supabase/permissive-policy -- explain why this is safe (at least 10 characters)
<the statement VibeGuard reported>
```

Use the comment syntax of the file: `//` or `/* */` in code, `#` in `.env` and YAML
files, `--` in SQL.

To turn the rule off or change its severity for the whole project, use `.vibeguard.yml`:

```yaml
version: 1
rules:
  supabase/permissive-policy: off # or: { severity: low }
```

See [configuration](../../configuration.md) and
[ADR-0004](../../adr/0004-suppression-design.md).

## CWE

- [CWE-284](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html): Improper Access Control
- [CWE-639](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/639.html): Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key
